scenarios.title: {J} Video Goes Viral for the Wrong Reasons
text: It's a twelve-second clip: {J} dancing in the car park an hour after a defeat. Context doesn't matter online. By lunchtime it has two million views and the club's media officer has called three times.
Someone filmed {J} laughing on the bench while the team was losing. He was laughing at something a teammate said about his boots. The internet decides he doesn't care.
scenarios.prompt: The internet is angry. Your response?

choices.label: Apologise publicly
choices.hint: The story dies faster. Some call it weak.
choices.text: The apology is four lines long and does its job. The club's media officer sends a thumbs-up emoji, which is the most warmth she's ever shown.

out.text: Silence works. A bigger scandal elsewhere buries the clip within days.
Silence is read as arrogance. A columnist writes a whole piece about “this generation”.

choices.label: Double down
choices.hint: Followers spike. Club and manager furious.
choices.text: The defiant post gets more likes than anything {J} has ever done on a pitch. The club fines him a week's wages. {M} doesn't make eye contact on Monday.

scenarios.title: {J} Faces the Press
scenarios.text: The club puts {J} in front of the microphones for the first time in weeks. The third question is the one everyone came for: “There are reports you're unhappy with your playing time under {M}. Is that true?”

choices.label: Diplomatic
choices.desc: “I trust the coach. I work every day.”
choices.text: The quotes are bland, which is the point. {M} gives him a nod in the corridor.

choices.label: Honest
choices.hint: Fans like honesty. The manager may not.
choices.text: “Honest {J}” trends locally for an afternoon. {M} says he respects ambition — through slightly gritted teeth.

choices.label: Pointed
choices.hint: Big headlines. Public criticism of the manager is costly.
choices.text: The back pages lead with it. {M} answers the next day: “Players who want to play should train better.” War is declared.

scenarios.title: Rival Fans Target {J} Online
scenarios.text: Derby week, and {J}'s mentions are a sewer. His mother's photo, edited. His mistakes, slowed down and set to music. One account has posted forty times in a day.

choices.label: Fire back
choices.hint: Huge engagement. Club won't like it.
choices.text: His reply gets screenshotted into every football group in the country. The club's communications team issue “guidance”.

choices.label: Report and ignore
choices.desc: Hand it to the club's safeguarding team.
choices.text: The club's team takes it over. Three accounts are suspended. The rest just find new ones.

choices.label: Take a social media break
choices.desc: Delete the apps for a month.
choices.text: {J} deletes every app. The first three days are strange. Then the silence feels like rest.

scenarios.title: Journalist Offers {J} an Exclusive Interview
scenarios.text: A respected journalist from the country's biggest sports outlet wants a long sit-down interview: childhood, family, ambitions. Two hours, photos at his old school.

choices.label: Do it, open up
choices.hint: People connect with stories. Some details get twisted.

out.text: The piece is beautiful: honest, warm, a little sad. Fans who never cared about {J} now do.
The headline twists one line about money into a story about greed. The rest of the piece is lovely. Nobody reads the rest.

choices.label: Do it, stay guarded
choices.text: The interview is pleasant and forgettable.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. The journalist writes about someone else.

scenarios.title: Popular Football Podcast Invites {J}
scenarios.text: A football podcast with millions of listeners wants {J} as a guest. The hosts are funny and ruthless. Previous guests have gone viral in good ways and bad ways.

ok.text: {J} is hilarious. One story about the academy becomes a meme. Followers double.

bad.text: {J} says something about a former coach that sounds worse out of context. The clip spreads.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. The podcast gets someone else.

scenarios.title: Fake Rumour: {J} Linked With a Big Move
scenarios.text: A transfer account with a big following reports that {J} is close to a move abroad. It's completely made up. But {club}'s fans have seen it, and they're asking questions.

choices.label: Deny it publicly
choices.text: A clear denial. Fans calm down. The account deletes its post.

choices.label: Post a cryptic emoji
choices.text: One eyes emoji. The internet loses its mind. {M} asks what {J} is playing at.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: The rumour dies in four days.

scenarios.title: Teammates Want {J} in a Dance Trend
scenarios.text: The younger players have a viral dance to film in the dressing room. They need one more person. The club's social team is very excited about it.

choices.label: Dance, badly
choices.text: {J} is visibly the worst dancer. The video is the club's most-watched of the year.

ok.text: {J} steals the video. Comments ask whether he should quit football for dance.

bad.text: {J} overdoes it and slips on a towel. That becomes the video.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: {J} sits it out. A day later the team loses and the video gets deleted anyway.

scenarios.title: An Old Post From {J}'s Teenage Years Resurfaces
scenarios.text: Someone has found something {J} posted at fourteen: a mean joke about a rival club's supporters. It's childish, not hateful, but it's spreading.

choices.label: Apologise sincerely
choices.desc: “I was a kid. I was wrong.”
choices.text: The apology is accepted by most. A few use it as proof of something.

choices.label: Delete and ignore
choices.text: Deleted, but screenshotted. It resurfaces every time he plays that club.

scenarios.title: TV Pundit Destroys {J} on Live Television
scenarios.text: A former player turned pundit spends four minutes of a highlights show dissecting {J}'s mistakes. “He's not good enough for this level. Simple.” The clip is everywhere.

choices.label: Respond on the pitch
choices.text: {J} says nothing. He screenshots the clip and uses it as his phone background.

choices.label: Clap back online
choices.desc: “How many caps did you win again?”
choices.hint: Popular with fans, dangerous with media.
choices.text: The reply is savage and perfect. Fans love it. Every pundit on that channel now has an opinion about {J}.

out.text: The pundit comes, watches, and changes his tune on air the next week. A friendship starts.
The pundit doesn't reply. The invitation looks a bit desperate.

scenarios.title: Charity Wants {J} as an Ambassador
scenarios.text: A children's education charity asks {J} to be their ambassador: school visits, a campaign video, a few events a year. No fee.

choices.label: Accept
choices.hint: Good for the soul and reputation.
choices.text: The campaign video makes his mother cry. Three schools get new libraries.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: {J} declines politely and donates instead.

scenarios.title: Fan Films {J} Refusing a Selfie
scenarios.text: After a bad loss, {J} walked past a fan asking for a selfie at the airport. The fan filmed it. The clip has a caption: “Fame has changed him.” {J} doesn't even remember the moment.

choices.label: Find the fan and make it right
choices.text: {J} tracks the fan down and invites him to training. The follow-up video is lovely.

choices.label: Explain
choices.text: Half the comments understand. The other half say excuses.

choices.label: Ignore
choices.text: It passes, mostly. It comes up again in every “arrogant footballers” list for a year.

scenarios.title: Gaming Stream: {J} Plays Himself in a Football Game
scenarios.text: An esports organisation asks {J} to stream a session of a football video game playing as his own club. Their audience is enormous.

out.text: {J} loses 5-0 to a fourteen-year-old, laughs about it for an hour, and gains a whole new audience.
{J} complains about his own video-game rating live on stream. The clip of him saying “my pace is NOT 72” goes everywhere.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines.

scenarios.title: Misquoted: “{J} Wants to Leave”
scenarios.text: {J} told a reporter he dreams of playing abroad “one day”. The headline says “{J} WANTS OUT”. The club's fans are furious, and {M} has read it.

choices.label: Release the full audio
choices.text: The full audio clears it up. The outlet issues a quiet correction nobody reads. Most fans get the message.

choices.label: Talk to {M} first
choices.text: {J} explains to {M} before training. {M} nods: “I've been misquoted too. Forget it.”

scenarios.title: Streaming Service Wants a Documentary About {J}
scenarios.text: A streaming company wants to follow {J} for a season: cameras at home, in the car, at training. The fee is huge. Privacy would be gone.

out.text: The documentary is a hit. Kids around the world now know {J}'s mother's name and his favourite food.
The edit makes {J} look moody and selfish. He didn't recognise himself.

choices.label: No
choices.text: {J} declines. They make a documentary about someone else.

scenarios.title: Reporter Asks About {J}'s Family Money
scenarios.text: In a post-match interview, a reporter asks if it's true {J} bought his parents a house. He hasn't, yet. He's been sending money home every month.

choices.label: Tell the truth
choices.text: “Not yet. One day.” His mother watches it four times.

choices.label: Refuse to discuss family
choices.text: “My family is private.” The reporter moves on.

scenarios.title: Fake {J} Account Scams Fans
scenarios.text: Someone has created a fake account in {J}'s name and is asking fans to send money for a “charity”. Several fans have already paid.

choices.label: Warn fans and refund the victims
choices.text: {J} warns everyone and quietly refunds the victims {cost}. The story of the refund goes viral.

choices.label: Warn fans
choices.text: The fake account is removed after three days.

scenarios.title: A Sponsored Post Turns Into a Scandal
scenarios.text: An online gambling company offers {J} money for one sponsored post. It's legal where the company is based. It's controversial everywhere else.

choices.label: Accept
choices.text: The post goes up and the backlash follows. The federation sends a letter. The club makes him delete it.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. Months later, three players who accepted are investigated.

scenarios.title: Fashion Magazine Wants {J} on the Cover
scenarios.text: A fashion magazine wants {J} for a cover shoot: designer suits, dramatic lighting, an interview about style. Football magazines never asked him that.

choices.label: Do it
choices.hint: New audience. Some old-school fans will mock it.
choices.text: The cover sells out. His teammates print it and stick it all over the dressing room with moustaches drawn on.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines.

scenarios.title: {J} Filmed Helping After a Road Accident
scenarios.text: On the way to training, {J} sees a motorbike accident and stops to help, holding a stranger's hand until the ambulance arrives. Someone filmed it. He's late to training.
scenarios.prompt: The club wants to share the video.

choices.label: Let them share it
choices.text: The video spreads across the country. {M} cancels the lateness fine before anyone mentions it.

choices.label: Ask them not to
choices.text: {J} asks the club to keep it quiet. It leaks anyway. The humility makes it a bigger story.

scenarios.title: Newspaper Rates {J} a 4 Out of 10
scenarios.text: The country's biggest newspaper gives {J} a 4 out of 10 in their match ratings. Everyone else, including the club's own data, thought he was fine. The rating is shared everywhere with crying emojis.

choices.label: Laugh about it
choices.desc: Post the rating with a joke.
choices.text: “Tough marker.” With a laughing photo. The internet decides {J} is likeable.

choices.label: Use it as fuel
choices.desc: Print it. Stick it on your mirror.
choices.text: The rating goes on the bathroom mirror. Every morning, a reminder.

scenarios.title: Should {J} Start a YouTube Channel?
scenarios.text: His agent thinks {J} should launch his own channel: vlogs, training content, behind-the-scenes. Other players earn more from content than from football.

choices.label: Launch it
choices.hint: Income and fame. Takes time and energy.
choices.text: {J} spends {cost} on a camera crew and launches. The first vlog does well. The fourth does better. It becomes a small business.

choices.label: Not now
choices.text: {J} says no. Maybe after retirement.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Channel Pays Out
scenarios.text: The channel has grown. The quarterly ad revenue arrives: {income}. More than some of his teammates earn from football.

scenarios.title: Journalist Asks {J} About Politics
scenarios.text: During an election season, a journalist asks {J} which candidate he supports. Every answer has consequences. Half the country will love him; half won't.

choices.label: Decline to answer
choices.text: “I'm a footballer. I want everyone to vote.” A perfect non-answer.

choices.label: Share your view
choices.hint: Love and hate in equal measure.
choices.text: {J} answers honestly. His followers split down the middle. Some sponsors get nervous.

scenarios.title: {J} Passes 100,000 Followers
scenarios.text: A small number on a screen, and yet it feels like something. One hundred thousand people chose to follow him. His first coach sends a message: “Remember the kid with the torn boots.”

scenarios.title: One Million Followers for {J}
scenarios.text: A million. The platform sends a verified badge and an automated congratulation. Brands start sliding into his messages. His mother asks if a million is a lot.

scenarios.title: A Columnist Has a Problem With {J}
scenarios.text: One columnist has written about {J} four times this season, each piece nastier than the last. Overrated, overpaid, overexposed. His colleagues say it's personal.

out.text: Coffee turns into two hours. The columnist admits he was harsh. The next column is fair.
The columnist writes about the coffee, too. Unflatteringly.

choices.label: Ignore him forever
choices.text: {J} never reads him again. The columns continue, unread by their subject.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Face Becomes a Meme
scenarios.text: A broadcast camera caught {J}'s face after a referee's decision: pure disbelief, mouth open, eyes wide. By Monday it's the country's favourite reaction meme, used for everything from exam results to traffic jams.

choices.label: Embrace it
choices.text: {J} posts the meme himself with “me reading my contract”. It's his most-liked post ever.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: It doesn't pass. Years later, people still send it to him.

scenarios.title: Children's TV Show Wants {J} as a Guest
scenarios.text: A children's television show wants {J} to visit: a football skills segment, a song, a puppet. His agent laughs. His mother insists.

choices.label: Go, and enjoy it
choices.text: {J} loses a penalty shoot-out to a puppet on national television. Every child in the country now knows his name.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. His mother doesn't speak to him for a day.

scenarios.title: Should {J} Talk Publicly About Anxiety?
scenarios.text: {J} has been struggling with anxiety for months. A mental health charity asks if he'd share his story to help young fans. It would mean admitting it publicly.

choices.label: Share it
choices.hint: Brave. Most responses will be kind.
choices.text: The post is honest and short. Thousands of messages arrive: kids, parents, other players. The weight lifts a little.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: {J} keeps it private but starts seeing a therapist. That's a start.

scenarios.title: Rival Player Mocks {J} in an Interview
scenarios.text: Ahead of the next match, a rival player tells reporters: “{J}? Never heard of him.” It's clearly a wind-up. The clip is shared with popcorn emojis.

choices.label: Respond on Saturday
choices.text: {J} says nothing until Saturday, when he shakes the rival's hand after the match and says: “Now you've heard of me.”

choices.label: Fire back
choices.text: The back-and-forth becomes the story of the week. Ticket sales go up.

scenarios.title: False Report Says {J} Is Badly Injured
scenarios.text: A gossip account reports that {J} has a serious knee injury. He's fine. But a club interested in him has just called his agent to ask.

choices.label: Post training video
choices.text: A video of {J} sprinting in training ends the rumour in an hour.

choices.label: Let the club handle it
choices.text: The club issues a statement. The gossip account deletes the post.

scenarios.title: {J} Nominated for Player of the Month
scenarios.text: The league announces its Player of the Month shortlist: five names, a public vote. {J} is one of them. The club's social team goes into campaign mode.

out.text: {J} wins the public vote. A small trophy, a big moment.
A bigger club's fan base wins it for their player. {J} congratulates him.

choices.label: Stay humble
choices.text: One modest post thanking the team. He doesn't win, but the post is the most liked of the shortlist.

scenarios.title: Invited to a Supporters' Club Meeting
scenarios.text: A supporters' club in a small town three hours away invites {J} to their monthly meeting. Forty fans in a rented hall, homemade food, one banner with his face on it.

choices.label: Go, stay late
choices.text: {J} stays four hours. He eats everything offered. Forty people will defend him online for the rest of his life.

choices.label: Send a video message
choices.text: A warm video message. They play it twice.

scenarios.title: Hate Messages After the Defeat
scenarios.text: After the defeat, {J}'s direct messages fill with abuse: threats, slurs, messages about his family. One account knows where his parents live.

choices.label: Report to the club and police
choices.text: The club's security team takes it seriously. The account behind the threat is traced. The police visit.

choices.label: Go public with the messages
choices.desc: Show the world what players face.
choices.text: {J} posts screenshots. The response is huge: support from players everywhere, a statement from the league.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Press-Conference Joke Lands — Too Well
scenarios.text: Asked about the next opponent, {J} makes a joke about their goalkeeper's hairstyle. The room laughs. The goalkeeper does not.

choices.label: Apologise with humour
choices.desc: Send him a hair product gift.
choices.text: {J} sends the keeper a gift basket of hair products. The keeper posts it laughing. The internet loves them both.

choices.label: Double down
choices.text: The keeper saves a penalty from {J} on Saturday and points at his hair. The internet loves that more.

scenarios.title: {J} Posts the Sponsor's Instructions by Mistake
scenarios.text: {J}'s sponsored post goes live with the brand's instructions still in the caption: “Write something natural here about loving the product.” Screenshots everywhere.

choices.label: Laugh at yourself
choices.text: The self-mocking follow-up does better than the ad. The brand renews his deal, delighted.

choices.label: Delete and hide
choices.text: Deleted. Screenshotted. Immortal.

scenarios.title: A National Football Legend Praises {J}
scenarios.text: On a national talk show, one of the country's greatest-ever players is asked about the new generation. Without hesitation he names {J}: “He reminds me of myself. Hungrier, maybe.”

scenarios.title: Fan Gets {J}'s Face Tattooed on His Leg
scenarios.text: A fan posts his new tattoo: {J}'s face, slightly wrong, on his calf. The internet wants {J}'s reaction.

choices.label: Invite him to a match
choices.text: {J} meets the fan after the match and they compare the tattoo to his real face. Neither stops laughing.

choices.label: Joke about the likeness
choices.hint: Funny or mean, depending on tone.
choices.text: The joke lands. The fan replies: “Not for long.” The internet loves it.
